place.id: Kec. Bahorok, Kab. Langkat, Sumatera Utara
place.en: Bahorok District, Langkat Regency, North Sumatra

scientific.id: Angin Bahorok adalah angin jatuh yang hangat dan kering (efek foehn) di sisi timur Pegunungan Bukit Barisan, Sumatera Utara. Udara lembap yang terangkat di lereng barat melepaskan hujan dan kehilangan uap air; ketika menuruni lereng timur, udara itu memanas secara adiabatik kering sehingga tiba di dataran Langkat dan Deli Serdang sebagai angin yang lebih panas, lebih kering, dan berhembus kencang. Angin ini dikenal merusak tanaman perkebunan, terutama tembakau.
scientific.en: The Bahorok wind is a warm, dry downslope wind (the foehn effect) on the eastern side of the Bukit Barisan range in North Sumatra. Moist air lifted over the western slopes sheds its rain and loses moisture; descending the eastern slopes it warms at the dry adiabatic rate, reaching the Langkat and Deli Serdang lowlands hotter, drier and gusty. It is known for damaging plantation crops, tobacco above all.

sources.text: American Meteorological Society, Glossary of Meteorology: “Bohorok”

curator_notes: SOURCE NOT YET READ BY ME: I added the AMS Glossary entry 'Bohorok', but glossary.ametsoc.org blocks automated access, so I only saw its wording quoted in search-result excerpts. Please open the link, confirm what it says, and cite it properly (it is a glossary entry, not research).

Per those excerpts the AMS entry also says: it occurs from May and is prevalent through September; it is feared for its effect on the tobacco plantations of the Deli plains; and there is more rain than usual on the windward side on Bohorok days. None of this is in the card text yet, because it is unconfirmed.

CONFLICT TO RESOLVE: the excerpts have the AMS entry attributing the wind to the 'east monsoon', while a European foehn-name list (EUMeTrain) reportedly ties it to the south-west monsoon. My own reasoning: the Deli plains are on the east, lee side of Bukit Barisan, which needs air crossing the range from the west or south-west, so 'east monsoon' may be an old name for the dry-season monsoon and not a wind direction. This is exactly the kind of point you can settle better than I can, so the card names neither direction nor monsoon for now.

Lead, unread: an Indonesian literature review on foehn winds (Jurnal Phydagogic, vol. 7 no. 1, 2024; ojs.unsulbar.ac.id/index.php/phy/article/view/3849) reportedly lists Bahorok under the Deli region. Its PDF could not be read here and the authors are not confirmed, so it is not cited.

Not found: no peer-reviewed study measuring Bahorok wind speed, temperature or crop damage turned up in my searches. If one exists it will help most; Indonesian journals and BMKG's North Sumatra office (BBMKG Wilayah I, Medan) are the places to ask.

Local knowledge: empty. Searches found nothing on the community's own account of this wind. Plantation-company records (for example the Deli Maatschappij) and Karo or Langkat Malay oral accounts are possible places, but this needs a named source; do not paraphrase from memory.
Local name: unknown. Is there a Karo, Langkat Malay or other name for this wind?
